marks.gloss_en: R' Yehuda: Babylonian kutach and all kinds of kutach -- it is forbidden to sell them thirty days before Pesach
one may not besiege gentile cities fewer than three days before Shabbat
והלא קצץ? -- but he has fixed a fee! [read after the fixed-fee clause, the Beit Shammai / Beit Hillel time limits make no sense]
הכי קאמר: ואם לא קצץ -- the time limits concern the case where he did NOT fix a fee (= p_rsh_hachi_kaamar)
Rav Sheshet: this is what it says -- and if he did NOT fix a fee, Beit Shammai: until he reaches his house; Beit Hillel: until he reaches the house adjacent to the wall
והאמרת רישא אין משלחין? -- but you said in the first clause one may not send [unless he fixes a fee]!
לא קשיא: הא דקביע בי דואר במתא, והא דלא קביע בי דואר במתא -- the seifa is where a post-house is fixed in the town, the reisha where none is (= p_seifa_kvia_bei_doar, p_reisha_lo_kvia_bei_doar)
this [the seifa, which lets him send without a fee] is where a post-house is fixed in the town
one may not send a letter in the hand of a gentile on Shabbat eve unless he fixes a fee for him
the mishna: these and those agree that one may load [on Shabbat eve] the olive-press beams and the winepress circles
תניא, אמר רבי צדוק: כך היה מנהגו של בית רבן גמליאל... שלשה ימים קודם לשבת -- the baraita reports the same custom of the Patriarch's house
ומדבריהם למדנו -- since white garments went three days ahead and dyed ones even on Shabbat eve, white garments are harder to launder
RSBG (mishna, cited by lemma): [my father's house] were accustomed... -- the elided remainder is the mishna's: to give white garments to a gentile launderer three days before Shabbat

אמר ליה: כבר קדמוך רבנן -- the Rabbis already preceded you: they taught that white garments are harder to launder than dyed (kind tanya chosen for the baraita source; the marker is כבר קדמוך רבנן -- header)
the launderer, asked what he wants for [laundering] the dyed garment: as for a white one
one may not set sail in a ship fewer than three days before Shabbat
דתנן: השום והבוסר והמלילות שריסקן מבעוד יום, רבי ישמעאל אומר: יגמור משתחשך
R' Yosei bar Chanina: the tanna [holding] that anything that comes about of itself is fine is R' Yishmael
one may put food before the dog in the courtyard [on Shabbat]
likewise, one may put food before the gentile in the courtyard [on Shabbat]
a person may not rent his vessels to a gentile on Shabbat eve
